messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: RStan status
parts:
RStan is done except for polishing up, bug fixes if found, and probably more documentation unless new functionality is needed. 

But there are a couple of issues.
1. I am looking the the effective sample size calculation now.  We need something that works not slow and supports one chain.
2. In stan/gm/ast_def.cpp and probably some other place, 
we have code that writes to standard error output.  R CMD check would report a warning (but not pointing out the exact place) for this. 

In addition, I am thinking of including boost inside RStan now as first I do not think it is easy for users of Windows and Mac (including Andrew)
to install something called boost into the system's header folder.  Second at least on Linux, I could monitor all the file IO, 
for example, for make test-all, so that I could get a list of all boost header files that are opened.  We might be able to downsize
boost header files from 100M to around 20M.  I am not sure this is a good idea and if I have not thought about something important. 

Last, I got rid of the symbol links used before as what works on linux is not working on windows.  So typical `R CMD build (and INSTALL)`
would not work now.  But I have a simple makefile in folder rstan, which could be used to build and install RStan before we could get it on CRAN. 

--
Jiqiang

If I remember correctly, CRAN made Malecki split mrpdata from mrp over 6 MB. So, I would guess they would have a problem with boost no matter how small we make it. I imagine most R users could manage if rstan would offer to open a web browser to http://www.boost.org/users/download/ .

Last, I got rid of the symbol links used before as what works on linux is not working on windows.  So typical `R CMD build (and INSTALL)`
would not work now.  But I have a simple makefile in folder rstan, which could be used to build and install RStan before we could get it on CRAN.

If the makefile route works, that is fine. But the symlink thing should work as well. As long as we do R CMD build rstan on Linux and upload that to CRAN, people who download the source from CRAN will get hard versions of whatever we symlink. It is only a problem for Windows people who download (R)stan from Google code. and try to build from source.

Is there any progress on LinkingTo RcppEigen rather than including the Eigen headers in RStan?

Ben

I just cleared those out. Right now, the
only place writing to std::cout is the command.

Will R be OK with that?

The parser fix won't be noticeable to anyone -- it
just involved passing references from higher up.

The bigger change is in the actual sampler. There's
now a method called

set_error_stream(std::ostream& o);

to set the stream to which error messages (like
domain errors in evaluating probability functions) are
written. The default's to not print them anywhere.

I then pass this stream down to the leapfrog algorithms
that need to report somewhere when they get an
exception evaluating the probability and gradient
(usually domain errors due to zeroes, infinities, NaN, etc.)

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan status
parts:
On 7/24/12 7:58 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
>
> Is it possible to pass an optional filename to stanc such that if
> specified, output is written to that file rather that std::cout ?
>

Yes. Use option "--o=<file>".

You can also do this by setting the name of the model,
which also changes the name inside the file. I couldn't
figure out how we'd want to do the naming, so I left
it flexible from stanc. It's easy to add other features,
too. Right now, it's pretty minimal:

~/stan> bin/stanc --help

stanc version 1.0.0

USAGE: stanc [options] <model_file>

OPTIONS:

--help Display this information

--version Display stanc version number

--name=<string> Model name
(default = "anon_model")

--o=<file> Output file for generated C++ code
(default = "$name.cpp")

- Bob
